channel.title: EU Foreign Policy & Sanctions Digest
channel.description: Daily digest of EU foreign-policy, Middle East and sanctions developments, framed for a Swiss reader.

item.title: EU FP Digest — 2026-11-27 (34 items)
item.description: EU leaders failed to agree the next multiannual financial framework at the Special European Council, where frugal states rejected Costa's compromise as too generous and cohesion countries defended farm and regional funds, putting the year-end deadline in doubt. The summit also exposed splits on Ukraine: Hungary, Czechia and Slovakia drew criticism for opting out of the latest multi-billion loan, and planned Friday talks were cancelled, leaving Kyiv's 2027 financing needs unresolved. On Russia, the EU added 15 entities linked to Russia's military-industrial complex to its Annex IV export-restriction list, which Bern should assess for alignment, and is weighing tighter export controls on "black mass" battery waste to keep critical minerals from being processed in China and re-exported to Europe, a measure Swiss trade policy may need to track. Leaders also adopted the Brussels Declaration with Western Balkans counterparts on enlargement and regional cooperation. Beyond Brussels, the ICJ's finding that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya has Israeli experts expecting a comparable ruling in South Africa's Gaza case, relevant to Switzerland as depositary of the Geneva Conventions, while Ukraine's push for stricter neutrality checks on Russian athletes and funding cuts to federations that admit them lands directly on Lausanne-based sports bodies.

item.title: EU FP Digest — 2026-11-26 (47 items)
item.description: EU and Western Balkans leaders adopted the Brussels Declaration at their 25 November summit, where von der Leyen and Costa framed enlargement as a strategic imperative, though the EU's push to make Montenegro its first accession in years now faces a resurfacing border dispute with Croatia. Hungarian PM Péter Magyar's meeting with Zelenskyy signals a conditional thaw after the Orbán era that could reduce Budapest's veto leverage over EU Ukraine and Russia sanctions decisions. This matters because the Russia sanctions pipeline continues to move: the EU added 15 military-industrial entities to its Annex IV dual-use export list, the Commission issued guidelines for a Schengen visa ban on individuals who fought in Russia's war, and a leaked draft package would target Russian sports and cultural figures used for propaganda. All three measures are relevant to Swiss alignment, and the visa-ban guidelines apply directly given Switzerland's Schengen association. Separately, the US administration proposed tariffs of up to 15 percent on Switzerland, the EU and China, and the Federal Council is awaiting official notification before responding, while North Korea is closing Switzerland's recently opened Pyongyang liaison office, reportedly over sanctions.

item.title: EU FP Digest — 2026-11-25 (51 items)
item.description: Washington has announced tariffs of up to 15 percent on Switzerland, the EU and China, part of a wider round that also targets Japan and South Korea and puts Bern and Brussels under parallel trade pressure; the Federal Council is withholding a response until it receives official notification. On Russia, von der Leyen announced a 22nd sanctions package, and the Council added 15 entities supporting Russia's military-industrial complex to the Annex IV export-restriction list, both measures Switzerland will need to assess for alignment. The Commission also issued implementing guidelines for a Schengen visa ban on individuals who fought in Russia's war, which bears directly on Switzerland as a Schengen associated state. Separately, Pyongyang closed Switzerland's newly opened diplomatic office and gave its head, Sylvain Astier, 48 hours to leave, calling Swiss sanctions on the Songdowon International Children's Camp a "blatant hostile act." In Brussels, von der Leyen told MEPs an energy ceasefire would test Putin's seriousness on peace and that a European team will join the next round of Ukraine talks, while a special summit on the next MFF exposed splits over its size, new own resources and Ukraine funding, with Merz demanding that all 27 member states contribute to Kyiv.

item.title: EU FP Digest — 2026-11-24 (26 items)
item.description: Commission President von der Leyen announced a 22nd sanctions package against Russia, including a proposed ban on Russian teams, flag-flying athletes and official Russian symbols at European sports events, which dovetails with a call from seven member states for an EU visa ban on Russian and Belarusian athletes; Bern will need to assess alignment once the Council adopts the package. The Council also added the founder of neo-Nazi network The Base to the EU terrorist list, subjecting him to an asset freeze and funding ban, a listing Switzerland would ordinarily review for adoption. Sanctions policy carries a direct Swiss cost in Pyongyang, where Kim Yo Jong threatened to close Switzerland's diplomatic office in retaliation for sanctions, putting at risk one of the few remaining Western presences in North Korea. In Serbia, the student movement won 140 of 250 parliamentary seats, ending Vučić's 14-year rule, though its factions are split between EU accession and ties with Russia, which will shape Belgrade's enlargement trajectory. Costa has convened a special European Council with a Euro Summit on 26–27 November 2026 to address the next MFF and Ukraine's 2027 financing needs.

item.title: EU FP Digest — 2026-11-23 (36 items)
item.description: Commission President von der Leyen presented the 22nd EU sanctions package against Russia, now before the Council for adoption, and the Commission adopted guidelines implementing a Schengen visa ban on combatants in Russia's war against Ukraine. Bern will need to assess both for alignment, and the visa-ban guidelines bear directly on Switzerland as a Schengen associated state. NZZ reporting that Russia's latest Geran drones contain Western-made electronics and likely Chinese components points to supply-chain circumvention the new package must address, with implications for Swiss export-control and anti-circumvention enforcement. In parallel, the Council adopted a €1 billion European Peace Facility measure for military aid to Ukraine, while Kyiv claimed sea drones sank the Russian corvette «Merkury» at Benghazi and hit a Russian freighter, extending its naval campaign into the Mediterranean, prompting a UN call for investigation and drawing attention to the Haftar camp's ties to Moscow. On the second tier, the Council added the founder of neo-Nazi group The Base to its counter-terrorism sanctions list, the HR/VP issued a statement regretting Tajikistan's withdrawal from the ICC Rome Statute (both candidates for Swiss alignment), the EEAS set an EU–Western Balkans summit for 25 November 2026 with North Macedonia still blocked by Bulgaria, and Costa's compromise on the long-term budget failed to win consensus.
